problem: The equation ${y}^{2}+16=-12y$ can be written in the form $(y+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $p+q.$

feedback.problem: The equation ${x}^{2}-4x+4=1$ can be written in the form $(x+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $\,p-q,$ and the sum of the roots ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-4x+4 & =1 \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot x\cdot 2+{2}^{2} & =1 \\ (x-2)^{2} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, $p=-2,q=1,$ and $p-q=-3.$

Now, we solve the equation using the square-root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2} & =1 \\ \sqrt{(x-2)^{2}} & =\sqrt{1} \\ x-2 & =\pm 1 \\ x & =2\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

We simplify the two solutions:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =2+1=3 \\ {x}_{2} & =2-1=1\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions are ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=1.$ Thus, the sum is $4.$
